response:
Your feelings aren't petty or selfish—they're real, and you're clearly working hard to make sense of them. What you're describing sounds less like being obsessed with material things and more like grief. You had a meaningful vision of these once-in-a-lifetime moments, and when they didn't happen the way you'd hoped, you lost something you can't get back. That kind of loss deserves acknowledgment, not dismissal.

Part of why it's so hard to move on may be that you're carrying it privately, hiding your disappointment and letting it leak out as anger over small things. That secrecy can keep the wound open. It might help to gently share these feelings with your husband—not as blame, but as honesty about what you're grieving so you're not alone in it.

Talking with a couples or individual therapist could also give you tools to process the disappointment and reconnect. You can honor these feelings and still build a marriage that feels meaningful. Both things can be true.
